Answers Josh's ask (Out/josh-to-leo-2026-09-28-press-conference-set-ask.md). 16 items, 8 after a win and 8 after a loss (a tie draws from the loss set). Each key A to D is right twice per set, and the right answer is never the longest choice. Practice-item shape plus 'after'. _label never renders. No real people, no names, no scores, no dates; 'move' never used. Port word for word.
intro_note: Asked at the podium after a game. after = win or loss; a tie draws from the loss set.

items.question: Great win today. Who gets the credit?

choices.text: The line. Every play started with them.
Me. I called every play out there, so I'll take this one.
Honestly, the other team just wasn't very good today.
Nobody yet. We should have won by a lot more than that.

hints: Which answer names somebody besides the coach?
Who does the work nobody films?
items.reasoning: Credit the people nobody sees. That's Be Kind.

distractors.B: Calling plays matters. So does everyone who ran them.
distractors.C: Knocking the other team makes your win smaller, not bigger.
distractors.D: A win is a chance to thank people, not to complain.

items.question: What do you want to say about the team you just beat?

choices.text: They should be embarrassed after a game like that.
Nothing. They don't matter to us anymore.
They played hard. They made us earn it.
They got lucky it stayed as close as it did.

hints: Which answer would you want said about your team after a loss?
Which one respects the effort, not just the result?
items.reasoning: Respect the people who pushed you. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: Embarrassing someone in public doesn't make your team look strong.
distractors.B: They're the reason you had to play well.
distractors.D: Calling it luck takes something away from both teams.

items.question: That's a winning streak now. What changes this week?

choices.text: Nothing. We've got this thing figured out.
We fix what almost went wrong.
We take it easy at practice. We've earned a break.
We'll worry about fixing things if we ever lose.

hints: Which answer still has work in it?
What's easier to fix: a mistake that almost hurt you, or one that did?
items.reasoning: Winning is the best time to fix things, while it's cheap. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: Every team you beat is studying how you did it.
distractors.C: Rest is fine. Coasting is how streaks end.
distractors.D: Waiting for a loss means waiting for the mistake to cost you.

items.question: Your backup came in late and made the big play. What do you say about that?

choices.text: Lucky timing. The starter is still the starter, no question.
Nice play, but don't get used to being out there.
Honestly, I didn't expect much from that spot.
They were ready when we needed them. That's practice.

hints: Which answer notices the work before the moment?
Which one would make a teammate want to keep working?
items.reasoning: Notice the work behind the moment, out loud. That's Be Kind.

distractors.A: Calling it luck skips the practice that made it happen.
distractors.B: Warning them off makes a good moment smaller.
distractors.C: Low expectations said in public stick to a person.

items.question: The fans want to rush the field. What do you tell them?

choices.text: Go for it. Nobody's going to get hurt out there.
That's up to them. It's not my problem.
Celebrate from the stands. Everybody gets home.
Only the bigger fans should go out there.

hints: Which answer thinks about everyone on the field, not just the fans?
What's the one thing that ruins a good night?
items.reasoning: A good night ends with everybody safe. That's Be Safe.

distractors.A: Crowds hurt people even when nobody means it.
distractors.B: When people are listening to you, it's your problem too.
distractors.D: Size doesn't make a crowd safe.

items.question: A close call went your way on the last drive. Was it the right call?

choices.text: Close call, and a hard job for the refs. We want to win clearly.
Obviously it was. The refs finally got one right for us for once.
Who cares? We won, and that's all that counts.
The other team always complains. Just ignore them.

hints: Which answer is fair to everybody on the field?
What would take the call out of the story next time?
items.reasoning: Respect the refs even when a call helps you, and aim to win clearly. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.B: "Finally" is a shot at the refs, even in a win.
distractors.C: How you won is part of winning.
distractors.D: Waving off the other team won't settle anything.

items.question: Your team turned the ball over twice and still won. How do you feel about that?

choices.text: Great. A win's a win, and that's all I'm looking at.
Those turnovers were on the receivers, not the plan.
Turnovers don't really matter if you win the game.
Happy with the win. The turnovers are on me.

hints: Which answer can be happy and honest at the same time?
Who does a coach point to first?
items.reasoning: Own the mistakes, even on a good day. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: A win can hide a problem until the next game.
distractors.B: Pointing at teammates in public costs trust.
distractors.C: The same turnovers against a better team decide the game.

items.question: Your student section was loud all game. Anything for them?

choices.text: They were okay tonight. Could have been a little better, I guess.
Thank you. The players heard you when it was close.
They should be a lot louder next time.
We would have won without them anyway.

hints: Which answer names what they actually did?
What makes a thank-you feel real?
items.reasoning: A real thank-you names what someone did. That's Be Kind.

distractors.A: "Okay" is what you say when you didn't notice.
distractors.C: Asking for more before saying thanks lands wrong.
distractors.D: Maybe true, but it takes a good moment away from people who showed up.

items.question: Tough loss. What happened out there?

choices.text: The refs cost us this game, plain and simple.
The weather was terrible, and it hurt our passing game all day.
Nothing, really. We played fine today.
We didn't stop the run. That's on me. We fix it this week.

hints: Which answer names one thing the team controls?
Which answer ends with a plan?
items.reasoning: Own it, name one fix, get to work. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: Blaming the refs means nothing changes on your side.
distractors.B: Both teams played in the same weather.
distractors.C: If nothing went wrong, there's nothing to fix, and the next game goes the same way.

items.question: What do you want to say about the team that beat you?

choices.text: They got lucky on a couple of big plays at the end.
They were better today. Credit to them.
They cheated. Everybody knows it.
I'm not going to talk about them.

hints: Which answer gives credit and still looks ahead?
Which one would you respect if the other coach said it about you?
items.reasoning: Give credit when you lose. It costs nothing, and it's true. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: Luck is the excuse that stops you from learning anything.
distractors.C: A claim like that needs proof, not a microphone.
distractors.D: Refusing to answer tells the room you're not taking it well.

items.question: Your kicker missed the last kick. What do you say to them?

choices.text: One kick didn't lose this game. I've got their back.
They have to make that kick. That's their whole job out there.
We might need to look for a new kicker.
I'm not going to talk about that.

hints: How many plays were in the whole game, besides that one?
Which answer would help that player show up tomorrow?
items.reasoning: Nobody loses a game alone. Stand with the teammate who's hurting most. That's Be Kind.

distractors.B: They already know. Saying it on camera only adds weight.
distractors.C: Moving on from someone in public, on their worst day, is hard to take back.
distractors.D: Silence reads like you agree it's their fault.

items.question: Your best player got hurt in the third quarter. Why didn't they go back in?

choices.text: Honestly, we should have put them back in. We might have won.
They wanted back in, so next time we'll let them decide.
You don't play through an injury. One game isn't worth it.
They were being soft about it.

hints: Which lasts longer: one game, or an injury?
Who should decide when a hurt player is ready?
items.reasoning: No game is worth a player's health. That's Be Safe.

distractors.A: A win isn't worth a worse injury.
distractors.B: Players almost always want back in. That's why an adult decides.

items.question: Three losses in a row. Is the season over?

choices.text: Yeah, probably. It's been a rough stretch.
No. We fix one thing at a time and show up Monday.
We'll just try harder, that's all.
It's the schedule. We've played the toughest teams in the league.

hints: Which answer has an actual plan in it?
What does "one thing at a time" do for a team that's down?
items.reasoning: A slump ends one fix at a time. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: Quitting out loud makes it true.
distractors.C: Trying harder at the same thing gets the same result.
distractors.D: You can't change the schedule. You can change how you play it.

items.question: Some fans booed at the end. How do you respond?

choices.text: Those aren't real fans anyway.
Honestly? Boo them right back.
Whatever. I don't care what they think of us out there.
They want better. So do we. We'll earn it back.

hints: Which answer turns frustration into something shared?
Can you respect someone who's upset with you?
items.reasoning: Take the frustration seriously, and answer it with work. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: Deciding who counts as a fan picks a fight you don't need.
distractors.B: Answering anger with anger makes the night worse.
distractors.C: Saying you don't care usually means you do, and it shows.

items.question: Your players look down in the locker room. What do you tell them?

choices.text: Heads up. One thing we did well, one thing we fix.
That one's basically on all of you.
Nobody talks until tomorrow. Go home.
Some of you didn't show up today, and you know who you are.

hints: Which answer lifts the room and still gets to work?
What happens when a team hears only what went wrong?
items.reasoning: Lift the room first, then fix one thing. That's Be Kind.

distractors.B: Blaming everyone at once gives nobody a way forward.
distractors.C: Silence lets everyone pick the worst story.
distractors.D: Calling out "some of you" in front of everybody hits the whole room.

items.question: Your team drew a lot of penalties today. What's the plan?

choices.text: The refs were looking for us all game, from the first snap.
Penalties happen. There's nothing you can do.
We clean it up at practice. It hurts the whole team.
A few players need to sit next game.

hints: Which answer treats penalties as something the team controls?
Where do fixes happen: in the game, or before it?
items.reasoning: Discipline gets built at practice, not in the game. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: If the refs were the problem, nothing gets fixed, and the penalties keep coming.
distractors.B: Most penalties come from habits, and habits can change.
distractors.D: Benching people doesn't fix the habit that caused it.
